title: BenevolentAI knowledge graph proposed baricitinib for COVID-19; randomized trials and regulators confirmed benefit
summary: AI knowledge graph proposed baricitinib in Feb 2020; ACTT-2 showed faster recovery and COV-BARRIER lower 28-day mortality (a secondary endpoint); FDA and WHO endorsed it.
account: On 4 February 2020 BenevolentAI staff published a Lancet correspondence reporting that the company's machine-learning-built knowledge graph identified baricitinib, a rheumatoid-arthritis JAK inhibitor, as a candidate against 2019-nCoV because it binds AAK1, a regulator of viral endocytosis. Randomised trials then tested that hypothesis. ACTT-2 (1,033 patients, enrolled 8 May to 1 July 2020) reported median recovery of 7 days versus 8 (rate ratio 1.16, 95% CI 1.01-1.32), and 10 versus 18 days among patients on high-flow oxygen or non-invasive ventilation. COV-BARRIER (1,525 patients) did not meet its primary endpoint of disease progression (27.8% versus 30.5%, odds ratio 0.85, p=0.18); its 28-day all-cause mortality, a secondary endpoint, was 8% versus 13% (hazard ratio 0.57, nominal p=0.0018). FDA authorized baricitinib with remdesivir on 19 November 2020; WHO strongly recommended it on 14 January 2022.
purpose: Drug repurposing: mine a machine-learning-built biomedical knowledge graph for approved drugs that might block a new coronavirus.
system: BenevolentAI knowledge graph (relationships extracted from literature by machine learning) with AAK1 inhibitor screening
deployer: ACTT-2 Study Group (NIAID); COV-BARRIER investigators (Eli Lilly)
segment: Hospitalised COVID-19 patients requiring supplemental oxygen or ventilatory support
taxonomy_note: Loose fit. The AI contribution was candidate discovery; the realized benefit was clinical (reduced mortality and recovery time), for which the fixed taxonomy has no health-outcome category.

ratings.reason: COV-BARRIER reported 28-day all-cause mortality of 8% (n=62) on baricitinib versus 13% (n=100) on placebo, hazard ratio 0.57, so treated patients who would otherwise have died survived.
ACTT-2 showed median recovery falling from 8 to 7 days overall and from 18 to 10 days for patients on high-flow oxygen or non-invasive ventilation, materially easing hospital burden.
WHO strongly recommended baricitinib for patients with severe or critical COVID-19 on 14 January 2022, making the AI-proposed drug part of standard pandemic care at population scale.

ai_role.statement: The AI's role was hypothesis generation only: BenevolentAI's knowledge graph ranked baricitinib among six high-affinity AAK1-binding approved drugs and the authors published the prediction. It did not design, run or analyze the trials. The demonstrated clinical benefit was established by randomized controlled trials (ACTT-2, COV-BARRIER) conducted by investigators unconnected to BenevolentAI, and judged by FDA and WHO.

Paired with AI Incident Database incident 225 (medium confidence); severity not given by the source.

Recategorised from specific harm prevented to 1 because the sources show an AI-generated repurposing hypothesis confirmed at cohort level by randomized trials rather than a specific harm prevented for an identifiable beneficiary, and, on the fact-checker's other findings, made the ACTT-2 quote verbatim, relabelled the Lancet correspondence letter as 'other', used the exact source titles, replaced the unsupported 'hospitals worldwide' with the trial sponsors as deployers, and stated in the summary and account that COV-BARRIER missed its primary endpoint and that its 28-day mortality reduction was a secondary endpoint.
